alex: Heads-up — we saw a ~2.3x p50 regression on the small-seqlen path after the driver swap at 09:02 UTC. Looks correlated with stale KV entries pointing at old kernel variants. :frowning:

maria: omg. did the deploy include the kernel-selector ABI bump?

alex: yes, driver 1.12.0 -> 1.13.0 (kernel-selector v3). runtime stayed at r-2026-03-10. The driver sends the new 'arch_hint' field, but cache keys on some hosts still lack the tag so selector falls back unexpectedly to a scalar kernel.

jon: can you paste the sample key that mismatched?

alex: sure — from pod runtime-7: 
```
KVKEY: model=redwood/open-7b:ver=20260301:seqbin=64:arch=a100:kernel=opt-v1:driver_ver=1.12.0
KVKEY: model=redwood/open-7b:ver=20260301:seqbin=64:arch=a100:kernel=slow-ref:driver_ver=1.13.0
```

alex: i.e. we have two keys for the same logical entry, and after driver swap the lookup picks the wrong one because selector logic checks arch_hint but not driver_ver.

suresh: that's bad. sounds like keying scheme needs to encode the selector contract version and model build id. otherwise persistence across driver/runtime transitions yields semantic mismatch.

maria: agree. quick options: A) add 'selector_v' + 'model_build_sha' to key namespace (breaking change but correct); B) keep current keys and add runtime-layer compatibility map to prefer newer kernel variants; C) invalidate-on-driver-change via tombstone sweep.

devon: pros/cons: A is deterministic but will cause a cold cache after every rollout (cost spike). B is complex and brittle. C is simple but may miss hosts where sweep failed.

jon: what did our canary show? infra-bot: deploy-cana ry finished — 60% traffic on canary, 9/10 warmups showed no regressions, but 1 host had old persisted DB leading to a tail latency spike.

alex: exact. failure mode appears when persistence older than rollout window keeps an entry with kernel tag incompatible with selector semantics. We need a migration path that avoids full coldstart.

maria: proposal: change key format to include 'selector_sig' and 'model_uuid' but also write a small tombstone index entry at rotate-time that maps old-key-prefix -> new-key-prefix for N days. Lookup logic: prefer direct key -> else check tombstone map -> if map points to newer key then fetch. Add async backfill to populate new keys from old ones where possible.

suresh: +1. must also version the tombstone format. add metrics: tombstone_hits, tombstone_misses, backfill_success_rate, stale_kernel_lookups.

devon: and add a runtime config flag: experimental.selector_compat_mode that enables the tombstone lookup for 2 weeks while we roll. default off afterwards.

jon: estimate effort? maria, can you scope migration job + runtime change?

maria: will do. rough: runtime change (lookup fallback + metrics) 1 week, driver key write change 2 days, migration job 3 days, infra rollout + canary 2 days. Total ~2.5 weeks end-to-end with monitoring gates.

alex: actionable: 1) implement key format change + tombstone write (maria) 2) add tombstone fallback logic + metrics (jon) 3) make migration job to scan old keys and backfill (suresh) 4) add runtime flag and rollout plan (devon) 5) dashboard + alert thresholds (alex)

maria: putting a PR queue item for runtime tomorrow AM. I'll include test harness that simulates driver/runtime mismatch.

jon: also add unit test that asserts kernel selection prefers kernel with matching selector_sig and falls back via tombstone only once, not repeatedly.

suresh: note: persistence layer uses RocksDB snapshots — migration should use snapshot reads to avoid locking. add retry logic if write conflict.

infra-bot: rolling deploy job started for selector-compat rollback watcher (job-id 98721).

alex: Thanks. I'll draft a short runbook for on-call: steps to force-invalidate tombstone map vs full sweep. :white_check_mark:

maria: cool. tagging @devops for storage quota watch (backfill will spike writes).

devon: I can add an opt-in telemetry flag to limit backfill rate (qps throttle).

alex: great. we'll review after the PRs land and schedule a dry-run on staging.

jon: one more: add profile sampler to capture kernel runtime histograms pre/post migration so we can prove perf recovered.

alex: noted. closing thread once PRs are up.
